scope: Re-review of frozen transport TTL/ownership and captured per-sink expiry accounting, carrying forward unchanged source FIFO/typed identity review01. No hardware, IDF build, flash, production edits, or commit by reviewer.
head: 8a1794ce3be95ff0007698c4e4e667dcf25fbe19

findingsResolved.issue: Owned retry could remain live beyond the advertised local TTL indefinitely while lifecycle/new protected work won every selection. Queued protected entries had the same priority-starvation exposure.
findingsResolved.fix: ReceiveNext performs constant bounded expiry housekeeping before selecting send priority. Retry is already task-owned after synchronous NO_MEM. Pending entries are first dequeued into local ownership (maximum two); expired owners are generation-checked and released; live owners are restored in reverse insertion order to preserve FIFO. No scan/reclaim of WRITING or SDK-owned slots.
findingsResolved.independentReproduction: Original publish/NO_MEM/50 lifecycle at100ms schedule repeated against frozen source. Owner exists before deadline, is retired at first dispatch at1s, remains absent at5s; all50 lifecycle records processed, one BLE failure/drop and no release mismatch. Saved02 fixture changes expectations and adds deadline assertions; current queue-stub boilerplate is explicit.

findingsResolved.issue: Intermediate expiry housekeeping released WiFi-only copies without WiFi drop accounting and falsely attributed two BLE failures.
findingsResolved.fix: Explicit protected-network-descriptor total TTL. Eligibility is captured at enqueue: BLE generation nonzero and WiFi enabled+ready. ExpireOwnedProtected snapshots these and WiFi-attempted state, releases only with validated generation, then counts one layer expiry and each eligible unattempted sink separately. No send/SDK/lwIP calls in housekeeping.
findingsResolved.independentReproduction: Identical original two WiFi-only protected publications then advance to1s: released2, wifiCalls0, wifiDataDrop2, wifiExpired2, bleDataDrop0, bleExpired0, layerExpired2. This accepts the documented TTL policy, not a claim of attempted WiFi delivery.

ownershipAndConcurrency: Dequeue gives exclusive pending descriptor ownership before deadline inspection; concurrent producer can supersede only a descriptor it itself dequeues. An inspected/dequeued owner cannot be reclaimed by scanning a stale slot state.

Protected pool and queue each have two slots; each temporarily retained live descriptor consumes a slot. At most remaining unheld slots can be published concurrently, leaving sufficient queue capacity for reverse-front restoration. Compile-time capacity assertion and deterministic producer-after-dequeue/producer-during-restoration regressions cover this invariant.
ExpireOwnedProtected copies target/done booleans before release. It accesses no payload after release, so immediate generation-changing slot reuse cannot restamp the retired record attribution.
WiFi attempted flag is set after both successful and failed synchronous submission returns; a retained BLE NO_MEM retry never repeats that WiFi attempt or accounts it as unattempted at expiry.
All normal, lifecycle, protected allocation and release paths clear protectedWifiTarget/protectedWifiDone; current settings changes do not alter captured expiry qualification.

Source FIFO, encoder-paired immutable identity and original full2304 protected bytes are unchanged from independently reviewed first revision. Normal capacity remains source4/transport4; reserved protection2 and lifecycle1 are separate. Formal USB source ordering is unchanged.

Lifecycle remains first send priority after housekeeping. The housekeeping performs at most one owned-retry check and two queued-descriptor checks; all queue waits are0 and no external send is introduced.
countersAndOrdering: expired counts each released protected network descriptor once; bleExpired/wifiExpired count only captured targets whose local copy has not been admitted/attempted. No captured target is not an invented sink timeout.
NO_MEM retryAttempts and per-sink terminal drop attribution remain separate. accepted/submitted counters are local API results and do not mean peer receipt.
A captured WiFi copy may be disposed at its explicit local TTL even while BLE is disabled. That disposition is independent of BLE success/failure and is now visible in WiFi drop/expired counters.

Before TTL, existing WiFi send ordering can be protected-before-older-normal; each carries original identity and bytes. No promise of UDP in-order delivery is introduced; BLE obsolete fence remains BLE-specific.
maintainedRegressionCoverage: Actual extracted source+transport, compiled pool and CVRM encoder, UBSan; source ownership/WRITING/50 configs, CRC/SHORT/full2304, lifecycle/newprotected/mixed expiry pressure, pending live-head/expired-tail, producer interleavings/FIFO, seven per-sink expiry classes, successful+failed WiFi-attempt retry, allocator metadata clearing.
residualLimits: No HIL/radio/performance acceptance is established by these synthetic scheduling tests. Board build, flashing, RF weakening and user fixture acceptance remain parent tasks.
The local TTL is checked when the Transport task can execute dispatch housekeeping; it is not a physical-time cancellation guarantee for an already-blocked SDK caller.

Existing WiFi normal/lifecycle send calls still reach lwIP mailbox/semaphore waits with portMAX_DELAY even though the outer socket send uses MSG_DONTWAIT. This patch deliberately adds no such call to housekeeping. See wifi-udp-sdk-deadline-source-review-01.json; do not claim all project P0/P1 risks closed or all SDK calls bounded.

BLE one-second snapshot due/miss and source/transport protected reservations are not a guarantee of completion or PC receipt. The separate BLE reviewer accepted bounded pending capacity under indefinitely higher-priority control as documented residual; this transport TTL is a different explicit local rule.
